programme.desc: George and Susan Master wanted to downsize from their 5400-SF territorial style home in North Scottsdale into a soft contemporary 3000-SF home. Though not a “small house” it was a significant reduction. In many ways, this has been more difficult to design a smaller plan that met all the needs of their lifestyle. There could be no wasted space and the scale and rhythm had to hit right on.

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: Have you ever wondered what it would be like to live in a modern home? A home where the line between inside and out is so blurred that nature sometimes comes crawling into your room. Are you afraid modern architecture is only for childless Avant guard art collectors who wear black turtleneck sweaters even in summer? Then take a moment to watch this Desert Wash video and see modern living through a child's eye. It will change your perspective about what site-sensitive modern architecture can be.

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: Fall is the perfect time to plan a full color landscape for spring. Let's face it, after a long winter we are starved for pops of color and bulb flowers are perfect. I show you how to quickly create a patch of color in your landscape in under 15 minutes.

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Sometimes we get a bit stuck in the past with heritage homes, fixating on the original build year and forget that the home and society has evolved over 140 years. Queen Bess Row was built in 1886, and ZGA Studio wanted to keep the heritage alive and relevant but in a more contemporary world. Subtle interventions were made during the heritage renovation, including the inclusion of a glass lift, but all was done to not only honour its past but also reflect how we live today.
programme.sub-title: Keeping the Heritage Alive in this 1880s Home Renovation

programme.title: Landscape Design
programme.desc: Vee takes you on a tour of her studio and nursery, including bees, chickens and some very cool plants. Learn how the senses: sight, smell, sound, touch and taste (plus the added bonus of time!) combine to create inspiring sanctuaries that uplift and connect you to nature.
programme.sub-title: Landscape Design : Bay Area by Vee Horticulture | Berkeley, California

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Architect Douglas Wan wanted something simple for his own tiny apartment, avoiding the fancy gadgetry often found in tiny homes. He thought about how he might want to live in the apartment, with the idea of living a monastic life but in the city.
programme.sub-title: A Minimalist Interior That Gives a Lesson in Tiny Apartment Design

programme.title: The Zero-Waste Home

programme.desc: SO, I wanted to build shelving for my kid's playroom closet and honestly, I could NOT find an easy beginner tutorial ANYWHERE! Then we finished our basement and I built both my kids closets out a year ago and gained some on the job knowledge.
programme.sub-title: DIY Closet Shelving - How I Made Shelves For Our Playroom

programme.title: Bold Backyards
programme.desc: This DIY raised planter is fully made out of cinder blocks! These blocks are staked and then filled with dirt and rock. Traditionally you would pour a concrete footing and then stack the block; I wanted to see if it would work with rock and block adhesive. I love how it turned out, and it's doing amazing so far. If I were in a more wet area, I would have installed a drain, we are in a pretty dry area, and this dirt is mostly granite, clay, and rock. I have found there isn't much settling that occurs in this area.

programme.title: Going Green Architecture & Design
programme.desc:
What will the buildings of the future look like? We took a trip to the Futurebuild Exhibition in London to find out exactly what our homes, offices, and schools of the future could look like. Come check it out!
This exhibition aims to bring together a number of different sectors in the field of sustainability. From engineering to construction, architecture, and conservation, Futurebuild looks to inspire the transformational change that is needed to push the industry toward net-zero by showcasing some of the most innovative materials and technologies that are making a breakthrough today.
programme.sub-title: The Future of Architecture & Design | Futurebuild 2022

programme.title: Going Green Architecture & Design

programme.title: Desert Architecture

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.desc: This project was all about the views. The Paradise Valley residence is located between Camelback Mountain and Mummy Mountain. Every space is designed around these views and creating wonderful indoor/outdoor spaces around these views.
programme.sub-title: Cámara De La Roca - Paradise Valley, Arizona

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: Settled into an upper Sonoran site in North Scottsdale’s Whisper Rock Estates development, the Anderson residence embraces a design influenced by Territorial style of the mid-1800s, as well as later Southern California rambling ranch homes. Both movements are sympathetically reinterpreted to harmonize with the beauty of Whisper Rocks Estates and the Sonoran desert.

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Architect Douglas Wan wanted something simple for his own tiny apartment, avoiding the fancy gadgetry often found in tiny homes. He thought about how he might want to live in the apartment, with the idea of living a monastic life but in the city.
programme.sub-title: A Minimalist Interior That Gives a Lesson in Tiny Apartment Design

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: Your master closet doesn't have to be huge to be functional. The key is well-designed storage solutions that best utilize every inch you have. The storage solutions that Sabine worked into The Greenwich House are no exception. Watch as she takes you through her design choices to create one amazing "his and her" master closet.

programme.title: America ByDesign - Architecture
programme.desc: Explore inspired spaces in this episode—from a tranquil wine oasis in Naples to a fire-resilient home in California, a reinvented Nashville library, and the High Line's iconic architect.

programme.title: Landscape Design
programme.desc: Specializing in custom garden design, award-winning landscape architect, Rhadiante Van de Voorde, principal of Elemental Design Group, shares her design philosophy for two unique bay area projects. This video features interviews and captivating footage to inspire the possibilities of design for your outdoor retreat.
programme.sub-title: Eichler Elegance by Elemental Design Group | Palo Alto, California

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: On a block measuring only 76m2 (818sqft), it was split in half with a pair of three-bedroom vertical townhouses, which meant they couldn't go 'out', so they went 'up'.
programme.sub-title: This Black Metal Townhouse Design is Inspired by a Handbag

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: Fall is the perfect time to plan a full color landscape for spring. Let's face it, after a long winter we are starved for pops of color and bulb flowers are perfect. I show you how to quickly create a patch of color in your landscape in under 15 minutes.

programme.title: Rise: Sustainable Home Tours
programme.desc: Meet Melissa and Jim - they built their dream home a few years ago, but this wasn’t like any other home. Their main goal was to have a healthy home for their kids, and one that would also save on energy and environmental resources.
programme.sub-title: Leed Gold Minneapolis Lakefront Home Tour

programme.title: Rise: Sustainable Home Tours
programme.desc: Welcome to the Passive House Ranch! Homeowners Beate and Bern have created a state of the art modern home while preserving the structure's original character. Their passive house has a classic ranch design with high-performance features that bring next-level comfort.

programme.title: Rise: Sustainable Home Tours
programme.desc: Passive House is an easy to understand building standard that takes home energy efficiency to a whole new level using 5 building standards that are explained in this video.

programme.title: Rise: Sustainable Home Tours
programme.desc: Are you still using natural gas in your home? Have you thought about the health impacts of doing so? Bruce Nilles--a Senior Fellow at the Rocky Mountain Institute--realized that his biggest carbon footprint was his own home.
programme.sub-title: Why Electricity Is Better Than Natural Gas In Your Home

programme.title: California Architecture & Design
programme.desc: Richard & Alix were looking to remodel the home that they raised their children in, and didn't know where to start. Alix is a watercolor artist and had a painting that she wanted in incorporate into the design of the remodel.

programme.title: California Architecture & Design
programme.desc: This renovation of a single family home in the historic Venice Canals presented the opportunity to reimagine the house. The ground floor was reorganized to an open plan, allowing all rooms access to the view and outdoor spaces.
programme.sub-title: Carroll House by Dimster Architecture | Venice, California

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: What defines good architecture and ultimately a well-designed home? If there was ever a perfect example it’s One MANI House by Mani Architecture. This home takes a difficult, narrow site and uses it to create an adaptable, flexible, four-bedroom home that is filled with unexpected moments, beautiful design details and lots of natural light. One MANI House brings good architectural principles to life.
programme.sub-title: This Home is The Definition of Good Architecture

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Living off the grid in a sustainable, comfortable home is a dream for many, that was certainly the brief that came to Ben Callery Architects. The challenge was to design something that could withstand the elements while embracing all the benefits of off-grid living. It was spectacular getting out to shoot Elemental House and for me, this project is a case study in not just how to live off the grid, but also what makes Australian minimalism.
programme.sub-title: A Home That Epitomises Off-Grid Living

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: If you have pets or delicate plantings, it's essential to install deer fencing on your property to keep deer and other animals away. But most often, fence installers place these in unsightly locations. I wanted an alternative and devised a more robust post to allow for greater spans of netting, rendering the deer fencing on my property virtually invisible. Have a look to see how I did it.

programme.title: Australia ByDesign
programme.desc: Episode 9 celebrates architectural brilliance across Australia—from the curved timber form of Burnie’s new cultural precinct to Melbourne’s Recovered Energy Centre and the urban revitalization of Sydney’s South Eveleigh.

programme.title: Australia ByDesign
programme.desc: From New Farm’s Chalk to landmark precincts, Australia ByDesign spotlights adaptive reuse, Country-informed design and materials transforming homes, schools and civic spaces across Australia.

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: The clients were looking for their forever home when they approached Winter Architecture and Field Office Architecture, and they wanted a home that could be intimate for their family of four but also accommodate entertaining large groups of people. With this in mind, the dining area became the central focus, with blockwork to ground the home and timber to provide warmth and softness.
programme.sub-title: A Family's Forever Warm Minimalist Home

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: Think modern architecture is stark, cold, better to look at than to live in? programme.title: Ideas For Your Home

programme.desc: George and Susan Master wanted to downsize from their 5400-SF territorial style home in North Scottsdale into a soft contemporary 3000-SF home. Then take a moment to watch this Desert Wash video and see modern living through a child's eye. It will change your perspective about what site-sensitive modern architecture can be.

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: It's the one room in the house that is truly the adult sanctuary and why not make it grand! From waterproof speakers in the shower, a luxurious bathtub, interesting vanity, and in-floor heating. The master bath at The Greenwich House has it all. Watch as Sabine takes you through her design choices for this relaxing and tranquil space.

programme.title: Going Green: Green Green World
programme.desc: Here are 5 new eco-friendly inventions which are saving the planet. This video includes sustainable, ethical, and vegan fashion companies that are creating products and technology to save Earth.

programme.title: Going Green: Green Green World

programme.title: Landscape Design

programme.sub-title: Landscape Design : Bay Area by Vee Horticulture | Berkeley, California

programme.title: Simple Dwelling
programme.desc: Winter Architecture was approached to design a renovation and extension to a two-bedroom Victorian home. Now providing four bedrooms and two bathrooms, the minimalist interior is filled with light from the courtyards, soft oak flooring and clean, crisp lines.
programme.sub-title: A Tired Victorian Home Turned Minimalist Interior

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: Home design trends are always changing. But, what is the right choice for your home? Sabine meets with Mahdad Saniee, architect at The Greenwich House to learn about some of the design choices that created such a unique and highly livable home.

programme.title: The Zero-Waste Home
programme.desc: Gittemary critiques ten trendy spring “must-have” items in this anti-haul, questioning their necessity and environmental impact. She suggests thrifted and DIY alternatives, showing how to recreate popular aesthetics without supporting fast fashion or excess consumption.

programme.title: Ideas For Your Home
programme.desc: It's the holidays, and Sabine has a few tips to make this holiday season a bit smarter, healthier, and greener. She looks at LED Christmas lights, a new outdoor smart switch from iDevices to automate all those outdoor displays, and how to use clippings from around the landscape to create unique and beautiful wreaths and garlands for your home. She also looks at a few natural and healthy ways to bring that classic holiday fragrance into the home.

programme.desc: This DIY desk is 14 feet long and made from wood and concrete.

I think this sustainable, sensitive house renovation by MRTN Architects showcases what can happen with true collaboration, as we see with the client's Martin and Cheryl May.
programme.sub-title: A Sustainable Addition That Is a ‘Shadow’ of the Original Cottage Home

programme.title: Woodworking For Beginners
programme.desc: SO, I wanted to build shelving for my kid's playroom closet and honestly, I could NOT find an easy beginner tutorial ANYWHERE! Then we finished our basement and I built both my kids closets out a year ago and gained some on the job knowledge.
programme.sub-title: DIY Closet Shelving - How I Made Shelves For Our Playroom

programme.title: Woodworking For Beginners
programme.desc: I'm gonna talk a bit about my miter saw, and try to give you a beginner's guide on how to use a miter saw.
programme.sub-title: Miter Saw - Beginners Guide, How To Use Miter Saws

programme.title: Bold Backyards
programme.desc: This DIY raised planter is fully made out of cinder blocks! These blocks are staked and then filled with dirt and rock. Traditionally you would pour a concrete footing and then stack the block; I wanted to see if it would work with rock and block adhesive. I love how it turned out, and it's doing amazing so far. If I were in a more wet area, I would have installed a drain, we are in a pretty dry area, and this dirt is mostly granite, clay, and rock. I have found there isn't much settling that occurs in this area.
programme.sub-title: DIY Raised Planter Box from CINDER BLOCKS.mp4

programme.title: Desert Architecture
programme.desc: After a mountainside home is devastated by a flash flood architect Brent Kendle AIA, LEED AP of Kendle Design Collaborative tears the lid off, as well as most of the walls, creating a new architectural vision of light, art, and forever views. programme.title: Austin Flipsters
programme.desc: Susanne and Anthony fully gut this house with plenty of surprises into a modern home you just have to see.

programme.title: The Inspire Action Podcast
programme.desc:
What does it mean to be part of nature, not apart from it? And how can an ancient philosophy guide us toward practical, systemic change in the modern world?
In this episode of the Inspire Action Podcast Ciara sits down with Dr. Simon Sadinsky - professor, Executive Director of Education, and in-house Harmony advisor at the Kings Foundation - to explore a philosophy that has guided cultures and peoples around the world for millennia, but is now finally being integrated into Western thought via a few key changemakers along the way. It shouldn’t be revolutionary, but it is in our world where progress often comes at the cost of the natural world around us.
Simon reminds us that Harmony isn't just philosophy - it's a practical roadmap for action. This conversation will hopefully shift how you see your place in the world, and remind you (as it did for us) that we all have a part to play in creating the Harmony our planet so desperately needs.
programme.sub-title: How Can We Reconnect with Nature? with Dr. Simon Sadinsky
